rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Registry-path strings can support a possible persistence hypothesis when the path resembles startup-related locations.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Command/interpreter strings support a possible execution capability but are common in benign administration tools.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Multiple conservative packing indicators can support a possible obfuscation/evasion hypothesis without proving packing.

rules.label: INFERRED
rules.explanation: Function-level correlation of executable memory APIs with relevant strings supports an inferred process-manipulation hypothesis.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Networking capability plus network indicators supports possible command-and-control relevance, but benign updaters may look similar.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Behavior evidence containing both DNS and outbound connection observations can support possible command-and-control relevance. Synthetic behavior remains low-confidence pipeline evidence, not a real-world observation.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Behavior evidence describing startup-like registry modification can support a possible persistence hypothesis. Synthetic behavior is provenance-marked and must not be read as actual execution.

rules.label: POSSIBLE
rules.explanation: Credential-related strings alone are weak evidence and only support a possible credential-access hypothesis.
